summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and coronary artery disease was admitted for worsening dyspnea, cough, and 6-pound weight gain following a recent upper respiratory infection. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, a moderate pericardial effusion with early signs of tamponade physiology, and elevated inflammatory markers consistent with viral pericarditis. He was treated with high-dose aspirin and colchicine for pericarditis, cautious diuresis with IV furosemide and oral metolazone, and a five-day course of antibiotics for possible pneumonia. His heart failure was managed with increased torsemide to 80 mg twice daily, and hydralazine was added for blood pressure control. The pericardial effusion improved without intervention, and he was discharged euvolemic with a plan for close outpatient follow-up, including repeat echocardiography and lab monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
